title: The Pop Clap
description: Build the clap-driven backbeat you hear all over modern pop and dance music.

steps.title: Why pop loves the clap
steps.description: Put on a modern pop song and listen to beats 2 and 4. There's a good chance you're hearing a clap, either on its own or stacked on a snare. The hi-hats are usually kept simple, and the kick moves around more, often landing just ahead of or between the beats. We'll build it up one piece at a time.

steps.title: The clap
steps.description: Hit the clap. In a lot of pop songs, this is the backbeat on 2 and 4 instead of a snare.
steps.hint: Bottom row, far left. It's the purple pad labelled CLP.

steps.title: Kick and clap
steps.description: Hit the kick and clap together. These two carry most pop beats. Get used to how they sound side by side.
steps.hint: The kick (KCK) is right above the clap, top left.

steps.title: Clap and hi-hat
steps.description: Now the clap with the closed hi-hat. That's how 2 and 4 sound once the hat is ticking along.
steps.hint: CHH is the green pad on the top row, third from the left.

steps.title: Stack the snare
steps.description: Hit the snare and clap together. Layering them gives you a fatter backbeat with a bit of both: the snare's body and the clap's snap.
steps.hint: SNR is the orange pad on the top row, second from the left.

steps.title: Kick, clap and hat
steps.description: Kick, clap and closed hi-hat all together. It's a full, punchy hit, good for an accent or the first beat after a build.
steps.hint: Kick and hi-hat are on the top row, the clap is bottom left. Close together in time counts.

steps.title: What's on 2 and 4?
steps.description: In a lot of modern pop, what takes the snare's place on the backbeat?
